properties.name: A prediction reads whether it was stated before the result it is tested by
properties.source: Anthony Sligar, 2026-10-28 ("continue working gap 3"), gap 3 of the design-a-phenomenon skill (#807)
properties.statement: When a result supports or contests a prediction, the read-back (reasoning_report, and the supporting/contesting reading itself) says whether the prediction was stated before that result was recorded, from times the server recorded rather than dates the caller typed: "stated before the result", "stated after the result" (post hoc), or "revised after the result" when the prediction's content changed after the result was recorded. The prediction's earlier wording stays readable. A prediction stated after its result is never refused and its reading of support does not change; the order is said, so a reader (or a journal reviewer) can see it. Designs with no results read exactly as before.
